senses.definition: A flat horizontal surface that you put your foot on when climbing up or down stairs.

examples.en: She sat on the bottom step and tied her shoes.

senses.definition: A particular movement of the feet that forms part of a dance.

examples.vi: Giáo viên dạy nhảy đã chỉ cho chúng tôi các bước cơ bản của điệu salsa.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English steppen, from Old English steppan (“to step, go, proceed, advance”), stepe (“step”), from Proto-West Germanic *stappjan, from Proto-Germanic *stapjaną (“to step”), *stapiz (“step”), from Proto-Indo-European *stebʰ- (“to support, stomp, curse, be amazed”). Cognate with West Frisian stappe (“to step”), North Frisian stape (“to walk, trudge”), Dutch stappen (“to step, walk”), Walloon steper (“to walk away, leave”), German stapfen (“to trudge, stomp, plod”) and further to Slavic Polish stąpać (“to stomp, stamp, step, tread”), Russian ступать (stupatʹ) and Polish stopień (“step, stair, rung, degree”), Russian степень (stepenʹ). Related to stamp, stomp.

senses.definition: To lift your foot and set it down in a different spot, or walk a short distance.

examples.en: He stepped out of the car and looked around.
examples.vi: Anh ấy bước ra khỏi xe và nhìn quanh.

senses.definition: To place your foot on or in something, especially by accident.

examples.en: Be careful not to step on the broken glass.

examples.en: I stepped in a deep puddle on my way home.
examples.vi: Tôi giẫm phải một vũng nước sâu trên đường về nhà.

senses.definition: To perform movements with your feet to music.
